fields.ic_name: AMBA AXI / ACE Protocol Specification (ARM IHI 0022E)

axi_baseline_security_inherited.name: AxPROT[0] Privileged
axi_baseline_security_inherited.purpose: Privilege-level signaling (User vs Privileged) at the bus layer.

ace_extensions_to_security_layer.name: ACPROT[2:0]
ace_extensions_to_security_layer.purpose: Snoop access protection attributes (mirrors AxPROT) so that snooped masters can apply the same access controls to snoop traffic as to direct AR/AW.

ace_extensions_to_security_layer.name: AxDOMAIN
ace_extensions_to_security_layer.purpose: Shareability domain partitioning — combined with TrustZone (AxPROT[1]), can be used to enforce that Secure-only data lives in a Secure-only shareability domain that excludes Non-secure masters.

ace_extensions_to_security_layer.name: AxBAR (Barriers)
ace_extensions_to_security_layer.purpose: Synchronization barriers can be used in conjunction with secure / non-secure boundary crossings to enforce ordering of security-sensitive operations.

ace_extensions_to_security_layer.name: DVM TLB invalidate scope
ace_extensions_to_security_layer.purpose: DVM TLB invalidates must respect shareability domain — a Non-secure DVM cannot invalidate Secure TLB entries (architectural rule; integrator must enforce).

what_is_NOT_in_the_spec: No confidentiality / encryption at the protocol layer (no AES, no cipher).
No data-integrity / authentication (no MAC, no HMAC, no signature).
No protection against malicious cached masters violating coherency invariants — the protocol assumes trusted masters within a shareability domain.
secure_integration_responsibilities: TrustZone partitioning: integrator routes AxPROT[1] / ACPROT[1] to Subordinate-side filters; non-secure accesses to secure regions returned as DECERR/SLVERR.
Shareability-domain partitioning for security: Secure-only data placed in a shareability domain that contains only Secure masters.
DVM scope enforcement: ensure DVMMessage broadcasts cannot leak invalidation of Secure TLB/IC/BP entries to Non-secure DVM targets.
Snoop-data path filtering: interconnect can drop or mask CD data on Non-secure snoops of Secure lines (architectural integrator responsibility).
WriteBack/WriteClean of dirty Secure lines must not be observable on Non-secure paths.
ACE-Lite IO masters (DMA / GPU) must be programmed to use the correct AxPROT and AxDOMAIN so that they do not bypass TrustZone or shareability barriers.
fields.notes: Security in AMBA AXI/ACE is limited to signaling primitives (AxPROT / ACPROT / Exclusive Access / Lock + shareability-domain partitioning) — not cryptographic primitives. ACE's coherency protocol does not, by itself, defend against malicious or buggy cached masters that violate the 5-state invariants — these are assumed to be trusted within a shareability domain. End-to-end confidentiality/integrity must be provided by upper layers (TrustZone Address Space Controllers, MMU/SMMU, dedicated crypto IP, secure boot ROM).

evidence.quote: AxPROT[0] Unprivileged/Privileged; AxPROT[1] Secure/Non-secure; AxPROT[2] Data/Instruction.
ACPROT is the snoop-channel equivalent of AxPROT, providing access-protection information on the snoop address channel.
DVM messages are distributed within the named shareability domain and must respect the Secure/Non-secure distinction at the system level.
